clue.text: Quiet 25's close relative employed in making buttons

parts.note: a mother is the closest of relatives, and the possessive turns the phrase into 'the mother of' what follows
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
the answer to 25 is a nobleman of the House of Lords, and an earl is one such nobleman

explanation.surface: A quiet nobleman's near kin finds work in a button factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does not give 25's own answer: it asks for an example of it, EARL. With P for quiet that makes PEARL, and the possessive ''s close relative' asks for its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, the iridescent shell lining, has long been cut and polished into shirt buttons.

clue.text: One may reach one's peak in this activity

definitions.text: One may reach one's peak in this activity

parts.words: One may reach one's peak in this activity
parts.note: reaching one's peak sounds like hitting the top of a career, but here it is literally arriving on a summit

explanation.definitionFit: Climbing hills and summits is the sport in which a person literally reaches a peak.

clue.text: Thanks to the Head of Classics, it's understood

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: the head of a word is its leading letter, so take the start of Classics

parts.note: it is taken as written, the 's being a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A grateful nod to the senior classics teacher is taken as read.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied or accepted without being stated.

clue.text: Welshman to note on the track, getting away very quickly

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name
E is a note of the musical scale
a scent is the trail a hound follows, a track

explanation.surface: A Welshman with a musical note races off down the running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' suggests a running track, but it is the trail left by an animal's smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescent describes something vanishing swiftly, fading from sight almost at once.

clue.text: Work after a month for one putting out feelers

indicators.note: after places the work behind the month in the answer

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: Someone sets to work after a month, testing the waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting out feelers' sounds like cautious enquiries, but it means waving tentacles.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-armed sea creature literally extends tentacles, its feelers, to explore.

clue.text: Security device father left in the yard

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left within the word for the yard

parts.note: a dock or dockyard is where ships are built and repaired

explanation.surface: A father leaves a security device lying in the back yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests a garden; here it is a dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock with a hinged shackle, used to secure gates and lockers.

clue.text: Chopper seen around many a centre of revolution

indicators.note: around means the word for a chopper wraps the Roman numeral

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crosswordese for many

explanation.surface: An axe is spotted near the middle of an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests a political uprising; it means rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns about a central rod or spindle, the centre of its rotation.

clue.text: A lad I once converted — lukewarm in religion

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged; it also plays on religious conversion

explanation.surface: A boy who once converted has since grown half-hearted in his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAD I ONCE is the fodder. The word comes from the church of Laodicea, rebuked in Revelation for being neither hot nor cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laodicean is half-hearted or indifferent, especially about faith, after the tepid early church of that city.

clue.text: Faust's sole beneficiary, do we hear?

definitions.text: Faust's sole beneficiary, do we hear?

parts.words: Faust's sole beneficiary, do we hear?
parts.note: the question flags that 'sole' should be heard as 'soul': the devil who gained Faust's soul in his bargain

explanation.definitionFit: In the legend Faust sells his soul to this devil, who collects it as his reward.

clue.text: Like some remote regions and unsuccessful pop songs?

explanation.definitionFit: Unmapped lands are unexplored, while songs that never entered the hit parade were never in the charts.

clue.text: Abandoned son in Cornish fishing port

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for son inside the name of the port

parts.note: Looe is a fishing town on the south coast of Cornwall, in south-west England
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A son is left stranded in a Cornish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' suggests deserted; here it means dissolute, as in loose living.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose in the sense of wanton or unrestrained, morally abandoned behaviour.

clue.text: It is swallowed up in the levy

indicators.note: being swallowed up in something means being contained inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something vanishes into the tax demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or income paid as a church tax, a form of levy.

clue.text: A supporter used on the set?

explanation.definitionFit: A beam that holds up a structure, and an object an actor handles on stage.

clue.text: Display mostly evoking an expression of envy

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle or display

explanation.surface: A show that is largely designed to provoke jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: A long audible breath can express longing or envy.

clue.text: Comment critically about talking bird on commercial

indicators.note: about means the bird's name is turned round

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of mynah, the bird that mimics speech
an advert is a commercial

explanation.surface: A critic sounds off about a talking bird in a TV ad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MINA into ANIM; 'on' just stacks it above ADVERT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is to pass censure or criticism on something.

clue.text: These exponents take great risks, covered by insurance

indicators.note: covered by means the risky gambles sit inside the insurance abbreviation

parts.note: to dice, as in dicing with death, is to take great risks

explanation.surface: Daredevils who gamble wildly keep themselves insured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponents' suggests practitioners; in maths it means powers.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra, the small raised powers in a term are its exponents.

clue.text: Desolate island without a flight

parts.note: desert as an adjective means desolate and empty

indicators.note: without means the following letter is removed from the island's name

parts.note: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A lonely island has no air service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desolate island' wants to be DESERT ISLAND; instead IONA loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the sense of running away, abandoning one's post or duty.

clue.text: Establishments where boxers may receive training

definitions.text: Establishments where boxers may receive training

parts.words: Establishments where boxers may receive training
parts.note: boxers here are not fighters but the dog breed, housed and trained in boarding places

explanation.definitionFit: Places where dogs are boarded or bred, such as the boxer breed.

clue.text: Ascetics' qualities do not include the first sign of charity

definitions.note: the possessive is a link to the rest of the clue; the definition is the plural noun

indicators.note: not including something means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: essences are the intrinsic qualities of things

indicators.note: the first sign is the opening letter of charity

explanation.surface: Austere hermits lack charitable impulses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Essenes were an austere Jewish sect around the time of Christ; the dropped letter is C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were a self-denying religious community living in the Judaean desert.

clue.text: Have qualms about very little at one time

explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate on moral grounds, and an old apothecaries' weight of twenty grains, a tiny amount.

clue.text: Rendered almost impotent as a result of Spanish peppers

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but the answer names the pepper as a kind

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters are reworked
almost means the word stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A man is left nearly powerless after eating hot peppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final T from IMPOTENT, and 'Rendered' rearranges IMPOTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet red capsicum, the Spanish pepper used to stuff olives.

clue.text: Animal captured and killed when eating a man's horse

indicators.note: eating means the word for a victim takes the name inside it

parts.note: prey is an animal hunted and killed
Alf is a man's name; the possessive is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A hunted beast is caught while devouring a fellow's mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A palfrey is a gentle riding horse of medieval times, ridden especially by ladies.

clue.text: Some soldiers are not dense

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
RE is the Royal Engineers, another British army corps

explanation.surface: A few soldiers are not stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some soldiers' gives two units, RA and RE; 'not dense' suggests clever but means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare air is thin, its molecules spread out rather than packed.

clue.text: Said of shepherds who renounce the past

indicators.note: renouncing something means giving it up, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: pastoral means relating to shepherds and country life
past taken as written

explanation.surface: It is said that shepherds turn their backs on history.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: East Ender's wife like Queen Wilhelmina

explanation.walkthrough: An East Ender is a Londoner from the East End, the Cockney heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney, 'my old Dutch' is a wife (from duchess); Wilhelmina was queen of the Netherlands.

clue.text: The main body, or just the chest?

explanation.definitionFit: The torso, the body without head and limbs, and a large box for storing or carrying belongings.

clue.text: Look closely at a bridge support, say

indicators.note: say means the word for the support is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a pier is a pillar holding up a bridge span

explanation.surface: Inspect the pillar under a bridge carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to squint or gaze intently.

clue.text: English poet said to be sound

indicators.note: said to be means the poet's name is heard, not spelled

parts.note: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman

explanation.surface: An English poet's verses are reckoned to be sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like praise for the poet; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially a loud one.

clue.text: It means endless trouble for Peter and Paul

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: It spells unending difficulty for the two apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetual means never ceasing, continuing for ever.

clue.text: Race for which garden centre has the finishing' posts?

parts.note: a nursery is where plants are grown for sale
stakes are wooden posts, here doubling as the race prize

explanation.surface: A garden centre's sticks wonder which horse race they finish.
explanation.walkthrough: A nursery stakes is a horse race for two-year-olds; stakes also means the prize money.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat race run for young two-year-old horses.
